authoredFrom: SQL-D17, 2026-10-21. The `extends` emission and the FOUR fabricated edges the pre-fix code published. The tree shapes were PROBED against the pinned wasm (`wasm/tree-sitter-sql.wasm`, sha256 in the spec's `grammar_provenance.pin`), not assumed: `ALTER TABLE child INHERIT parent;` parses to (alter_table (keyword_alter) (keyword_table) (object_reference name:(identifier)) (add_column (column_definition name:(identifier "INHERIT") custom_type:(object_reference name:(identifier "parent"))))); `ALTER TABLE c ADD COLUMN inherit int;` parses to the IDENTICAL shape with (keyword_add) (keyword_column) in front of the column_definition; `ALTER TABLE child NO INHERIT parent;` parses to (alter_table … (ERROR (keyword_no)) (add_column (column_definition name:(identifier "INHERIT") custom_type:(object_reference name:(identifier "parent"))))). The corpus contributes NOTHING to this fixture: measured over the whole admitted population (2,125 .sql files, 202 repositories, 199 symlinked directories followed, 0 parse failures), every textual `inherit`/`inherits` occurrence is inside a COMMENT or a psql `\echo` string — 19 occurrences in 17 lines across 10 files, 0 statements, 0 `keyword_inherits` nodes, 0 `ALTER TABLE … INHERIT` triggers. So the type is ZERO-SITES on the corpus and this fixture is the only place the construct exists.
comment: THE FORBID ROWS ARE THE SUBSTANCE. Before 2026-10-21 the `extends` rule keyed on the mis-parsed column's NAME and took the mis-parse's `custom_type` as the parent table, so FOUR legal SQL statements published a fabricated edge: a column literally named `inherit` (legal — `inherit` is NON-RESERVED in PostgreSQL, Table C.1 of the keyword appendix), the same column with a custom type, `ADD` without `COLUMN`, and `NO INHERIT` — the clause that REMOVES the relation, which the old rule asserted as if it created it. Measured before/after on the same probes: before = 4 fabricated edges, after = 0, with the one positive control unchanged. The `inherit` symbol rows are the other half: the old reserved-name guard DELETED a legal column, and the fix publishes it back with its real type. The `INHERITS`-on-CREATE-TABLE row is a pin on a LIMIT — that clause error-recovers to a top-level (ERROR) whose only children are "INHERITS" "(" ")", the parent name does not survive, and no edge may name it.
